concepts.definition: the organized sequence of events and actions that make up a literary work
a person, animal, or figure represented as taking part in the events of a literary work
the time, place, and social environment in which the events of a literary work occur
a central idea or insight explored repeatedly through a literary work
a struggle between opposing forces that drives action or tension in a literary work
a direct comparison that describes one thing as another without using like or as
a comparison between unlike things that commonly uses like or as
a contrast between what is expected or stated and what actually happens or is meant
the voice or perspective through which a story is told
a grouped set of lines in a poem separated from other groups by space or structure
